correctness.rationale: The sum and difference modes are orthogonal and have the same token normalization. At relative variable t=(1-c)/(1+c), the unnormalized sum multiplier is 1-η and the difference multiplier is 1-ητ(t)>0, with τ(t)=tanh(κt/(1+t)). Thus t'=t[(1-ητ)/|1-η|]² and the ordered vector result retains both orientation signs. At η=1 a noncollinear pair becomes antipodal exactly. For 1<η≤2, 2ηtτ'≤κ<1-ητ, so the scalar map is strictly increasing; the ratio t'/t is strictly decreasing. Comparing it with one proves monotone escape to infinity below or at η_a, trapping and convergence to the unique interior fixed t* above η_a and below 2, and monotone decrease to zero at 2. For η<1 the ratio is greater than one throughout. The interior derivative is strictly between zero and one, and the actual orbit is the signed swap (x1,x2)→(-x2,-x1), not an ordinary swap. The monotonic alternatives exclude additional cycles. Consensus is fixed, undefined, or sign-flipping as stated across η=1; the antipodal multiplier stays positive. At η_a, t'/t=1+4κ(1+tanh κ)/t+O(t^-2); at 2, 1/t'-1/t=4κ+O(t). Averaging these increments and using 1+c=2/(1+t) and 1-c=2t/(1+t) yields both constants for every noncollinear initial pair. Numerical diagnostics are supplementary, not the proof.
residual_risks: No formal verification claimed. No inference outside the stated two-token parameter range or to convergence of directions across different initial invariant planes.
